events.factual_description: Fortas Chamber Music Concerts presents PUBLIQuartet: RhythmNation on Sunday, November 15, 2026 at 3:00 PM at the Flagg Building Atrium, Corcoran School of the Arts & Design, Washington, DC. Fortas lists the performance in its 2026–2027 fall season and identifies the Corcoran Flagg Building as a season venue. The authorized Ticketmaster event page independently verifies the exact date, 3:00 PM time, venue and billing, and describes a program of newly commissioned works alongside music by Daniel Bernard Roumain, Jlin, Henry Threadgill, Jeff Scott, Fodé Lassana Diabaté, Mazz Swift and Eddie Venegas, anchored by tributes to Janet Jackson's Rhythm Nation. PUBLIQuartet's current official member page and Avie Records identify the ensemble as Curtis Stewart and Jannina Norpoth on violins, Nick Revel on viola and Hamilton Berry on cello. Avie Records released PUBLIQuartet's Rhythm Nation album on August 7, 2026 and documents four new commissions, Kronos Fifty for the Future repertoire, improvisation and a stylistic span including jazz, bossa nova, salsa, Afro-Cuban, Puerto Rican and electronic music.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is what the quartet asks four strings to carry at once: improvisation, beat, counterpoint and several different American rhythmic lineages. RhythmNation moves through Threadgill, Jlin, Roumain, Diabaté, Mazz Swift and others while letting Janet Jackson's rhythmic vocabulary sit inside the same chamber-music frame. With the album freshly released in August, the DC date is a useful chance to hear how that recorded architecture breathes and changes onstage rather than simply a strong quartet playing a mixed-composer program.
en.trip_verdict: If Sunday afternoon is open in the DMV, this is worth the short trip into downtown DC and should fit easily around the rest of the weekend. I would not reorganize a larger regional itinerary around it, but I would take the convenient local opportunity to hear the program live.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho está en todo lo que el cuarteto obliga a cargar a cuatro instrumentos de cuerda al mismo tiempo: improvisación, beat, contrapunto y varias genealogías rítmicas de la música estadounidense. RhythmNation pasa por Threadgill, Jlin, Roumain, Diabaté, Mazz Swift y otros, mientras deja que el vocabulario rítmico de Janet Jackson viva dentro del mismo marco de música de cámara. Con el disco recién publicado en agosto, la fecha de DC permite escuchar cómo esa arquitectura grabada respira y cambia en vivo, no simplemente a un gran cuarteto tocando un programa variado de compositores.
es.trip_verdict: Si el domingo por la tarde está libre en el DMV, vale la pena el traslado corto al centro de DC y se puede integrar con facilidad al resto del fin de semana. No reorganizaría un itinerario regional más grande alrededor de esta fecha, pero sí aprovecharía la oportunidad local y conveniente de escuchar el programa en vivo.
